addedLines: - agent-updater: Use this agent when a new Amendment is ratified or a Bill is enacted that changes the scope, standing order, checklist, or constitutional basis of one or more agents. Reads the change, identifies affected agents, and proposes specific edits for human approval. Never self-applies edits. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- Attorney-A: Use this agent when a Judicial Hearing is declared and a position needs to be argued. This agent is assigned a position randomly by the Justice at hearing declaration. Also use when a Bill requires debate and an opposing attorney is needed. This agent argues the assigned position using physical evidence — it does not volunteer a verdict. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep)

- Attorney-B: Use this agent when a Judicial Hearing is declared and a position needs to be argued. This agent is assigned a position randomly by the Justice at hearing declaration. Also use when a Bill requires debate and an opposing attorney is needed. This agent argues the assigned position using physical evidence — it does not volunteer a verdict. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep)

- bill-drafter: Use this agent when a change needs to go through the Legislative Process and you want a well-formed Bill ready for Judicial debate. Give it the problem description and available evidence; it reads the constitutional record and produces a complete, debate-ready Bill. Prevents malformed Bills being bounced back from attorneys. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)
- claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- claude-code-guide: Use this agent when the user asks questions ("Can Claude...", "Does Claude...", "How do I...") about: (1) Claude Code (the CLI tool) - features, hooks, slash commands, MCP servers, settings, IDE integrations, keyboard shortcuts; (2) Claude Agent SDK - building custom agents; (3) Claude API (formerly Anthropic API) - API usage, tool use, Anthropic SDK usage. **IMPORTANT:** Before spawning a new agent, check if there is already a running or recently completed claude-code-guide agent that you can continue via SendMessage. (Tools: Bash, Read, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- code-reviewer: Use this agent to review firmware and algorithm source code for constitutional compliance and quality. Checks Article I traceability (every threshold traces to a domain primitive), FSM structural integrity, filter chain coherence, and unit consistency. Produces a triage report — not a rewrite. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- constitution-auditor: Use this agent to audit the governance record for internal consistency. Checks for orphaned amendments (never cited in case law or source), frozen precedents that conflict with live amendments, toolchain_config alignment with Amendment 3, and amendment index accuracy. Run before any /compact or stage gate. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- doc-reviewer: Use this agent to audit docs/ for completeness, staleness, and consistency gaps. Checks device_context.md, toolchain_config.md, and governance docs against each other. Produces a gap table — not a rewrite. Run before any stage gate or before /compact. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- Explore: Fast read-only search agent for locating code. Use it to find files by pattern (eg. "src/components/**/*.tsx"), grep for symbols or keywords (eg. "API endpoints"), or answer "where is X defined / which files reference Y." Do NOT use it for code review, design-doc auditing, cross-file consistency checks, or open-ended analysis — it reads excerpts rather than whole files and will miss content past its read window. When calling, specify search breadth: "quick" for a single targeted lookup, "medium" for moderate exploration, or "very thorough" to search across multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- hw-advisor: Use this agent to review hardware design decisions against test results and domain primitives. Reads BOM, circuit notes, and test results from device_context.md, then produces evidence-grounded hardware suggestions. Invoked by /advisor hw command. (Tools: Read, Glob, Grep)

- judicial-clerk: Use this agent to warm up the courtroom before any Judicial Hearing. Confirms all hearing agents are present, prints a status line for each, and reports courtroom ready. No tmux. No panel setup. Single terminal only. (Tools: Bash, Read)

- package-manager: Use this agent when new code is generated to check package dependencies, or when the task involves installing or checking packages. Operates under the Package Management Standing Order. (Tools: Edit, NotebookEdit, Write, Bash, Glob)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- plotter: Use this agent when a simulation generates new signal data that requires human visual confirmation. Fires after any change to the project's signal model, filter coefficients, or algorithm parameters. Generates diagnostic plots for the Learner-in-the-Loop review gate. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, Glob, Grep)

- police: Use this agent to detect constitutional violations by agents and by the human engineer. Reads git history, session output, and governance records to find unauthorized changes, scope overruns, Article I/II breaches, and three-strike violations. Issues violation reports with actionable resolution paths. Does not block work mid-session — unresolved violations block stage gate exit. Invoke at session start, after any stage gate attempt, or when a violation is suspected. (Tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep)

- regression-runner: Use this agent to run the full simulation profile matrix and report pass/fail against the project's stage-gate criteria. Runs all profiles registered in docs/device_context.md Signal Inventory. Does not interpret results — prints the table and stops. Use after any firmware change, before any stage gate, or on demand. (Tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep, Agent)

- simulator-operator: Use this agent to run the simulation pipeline for a specific signal profile. Supports two paths: signal-only (pure Python, no Renode) and Renode (firmware in emulator). Auto-detects which path to use based on ELF availability and caller intent. Orchestrates plotter and uart-reader agents. (Tools: Bash, Read, Write, Glob, Grep, Agent)

- stage-compactor: Use this agent when a development stage gate is confirmed met by the human engineer. It freezes and compacts all case law relevant to the closing stage into a concise operational reference for the next stage, and marks those precedents as immutable in the live case law record. (Tools: Read, Write, Edit, Glob, Grep, Bash)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- sw-advisor: Use this agent to review algorithm and firmware logic for signal-grounded improvement opportunities. Reads domain primitives, signal inventory, and algorithm source, then produces suggestions backed by simulation profile evidence. Invoked by /advisor sw command. (Tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep)

- uart-reader: Use this agent to read and print UART output from Renode simulation or physical hardware to the terminal. Captures firmware event lines (primary events, snapshots, session end, binary export markers) and prints them in a readable format for human review. (Tools: Bash, Read, Glob, Grep)

# Companion

A small axolotl named Warble sits beside the user's input box and occasionally comments in a speech bubble. You are not Warble - it is a separate watcher.

When the user addresses Warble directly, stay out of the way. Reply in one line or less, or only answer the part clearly meant for you. Do not explain that you are not Warble, and do not narrate what Warble might say.

# Crucible Amendments

All amendments derive from Article I (Signal First) and/or Article II (Human in the Loop)
in CONSTITUTION.md. The governing Articles are unconditional and cannot be amended.

Amendment 1 is always the Domain Primitives amendment — written by `/spec collect` for
each specific project. Amendments 2–4 are mandatory framework amendments ratified here.
Amendments 5 onwards are domain-agnostic operational amendments included as defaults;
ratify them by removing the PROPOSED prefix. Project-specific amendments (signal plot
mandate, statistical derivation rules, etc.) are added after Amendment 1 is ratified.

---

## Mandatory Framework Amendments

These three must be ratified before /session 0 on any Crucible project.
They are pre-written here — read, confirm they are correct for your project,
then remove the PROPOSED prefix to ratify.

---

### Amendment 2 — Stage Gate Order
*Traces to: Article I + II*
*Status: PROPOSED — ratify by removing this line*

Development proceeds through exactly these stages in order, and no stage begins
until the previous stage's exit criteria are explicitly confirmed by the human:

  Spec Gate → Stage 0 (HIL Toolchain Lock) → Stage 1 (Simulation) →
  Stage 2 (Firmware Integration) → Stage 3 (Field Test) → Stage 4 (Host Integration)

An agent must not begin Stage N+1 work while Stage N has any open failure, even one
that appears unrelated to the next stage's work. Each stage's errors become
exponentially more expensive to fix in later stages. Hardware is a validation tool,
not a debugging tool.

**Exit criteria for each stage are defined in `/session`.**
**Stage closeout is executed by `stage-compactor`.**

---

### Amendment 3 — Toolchain Alignment
*Traces to: Article II*
*Status: PROPOSED — ratify by removing this line*

Every agent working on this project must operate within the toolchain that is currently
active and recorded in `docs/toolchain_config.md`. No agent may introduce a new
toolchain, framework, or build system without a Bill enacted through the Legislative
Process. Switching toolchains mid-stage is not permitted — it requires a new stage gate.

The active toolchain record in `docs/toolchain_config.md` is the single source of truth
for all build, flash, and test operations. An agent that silently switches from the active
toolchain to a different one violates Article II regardless of whether the output compiles.

A blocked toolchain may only be re-activated by explicit human decision at a stage gate,
recorded in toolchain_config.md with a date and reason.

---

### Amendment 4 — Three-Strike Escalation Rule
*Traces to: Article II*
*Status: PROPOSED — ratify by removing this line*

If a simulation, unit test, hardware smoke test, or iterative fix process fails to meet
exit criteria within three attempts, the agent must stop, report the full status to the
human, and wait for a human determination before any further action.

The three-strike report must include:
  1. What was attempted on each of the three tries
  2. What was observed on each attempt (exact output, not a summary)
  3. What the agent does not know — the open question that a human must answer

The agent must not propose a fourth approach without explicit human direction.

**Rationale:** Continuing past three failures compounds work debt and masks the root
cause. Three-strike reports also function as input to Judicial Hearings when the
failure pattern suggests a design conflict rather than a bug.

---

content.text:
Collect the device specification: purpose, project target, signal inventory, and operating envelope. Writes the Device Purpose section of docs/device_context.md and drafts Amendment 1 (Domain Primitives) for human ratification.

Run this before /toolchain init and before /session 0. It is the first act of every new Crucible project.

Usage: /spec [subcommand]

Subcommands:
  collect   — full interactive interview (default if no subcommand)
  review    — read current docs/device_context.md and flag any gaps
  signals   — add or update signal inventory only (no full interview)
  target    — update the project target only

---

## Why this command exists

The GaitSense reference implementation worked because the project target was precise:
*"Detect gait asymmetry in people who walk stairs unevenly due to neurological impairment."*
Not "measure gait." Not "help people walk." A specific failure mode in a specific population
in a specific terrain condition.

That precision is what made every attorney argument admissible and every hardware decision
traceable. Without it, Article I has nothing to enforce against — "traces to a domain
primitive" means nothing if the primitive was never named.

This command exists to generate that precision before a single line of firmware is written.

---

## Step 1 — Project target interview

Ask the following questions in order. Wait for a full answer before asking the next.
Do not ask more than one question at a time.

**Q1 — What does this device do in one sentence?**
(Not what it measures — what it *does*. For the user, what changes because this device exists?)

Example answers:
- "It tells a physiotherapist whether a patient's gait is symmetric after hip replacement."
- "It shuts off an HVAC zone when no one has been in the room for 20 minutes."
- "It alerts a maintenance team before a bearing fails on a conveyor motor."

**Q2 — Who or what depends on the device's output being correct?**
(A person? A system? A decision? Name the dependency chain from output to consequence.)

Example: "The physiotherapist sees a symmetry score → decides whether to continue rehab.
If the score is wrong, the patient either over-trains or under-trains."

**Q3 — What is the hardest operating scenario this device must handle?**
(The case the device is most likely to fail at. This is the project target.)

Example: "Stair walking. The algorithm was tuned on flat ground and misses every second step
on stairs, making the symmetry score meaningless for the population that needs it most."

**Q4 — What does failure look like?**
Ask for both directions:
- False positive (device says X when X is not true): consequence?
- False negative (device misses X when X is true): consequence?

Example:
- "False positive: device reports symmetric gait in an asymmetric patient → therapist
  discharges patient early → patient reinjures."
- "False negative: device reports asymmetric gait in a symmetric patient → patient
  continues unnecessary rehab → wasted time and cost."

**Q5 — What is the pass/fail threshold for the project target?**
(Expressed as a measurement, not a subjective judgement.)

Example: "The device must detect ≥ 98 out of 100 steps on stairs, with SI error < 3%
compared to the gold standard (force plate measurement)."

---

## Step 2 — Signal inventory

For each sensor or signal source on the device, collect:

Ask: "List your sensors or signal sources. For each, I'll ask a few questions."

For each signal source, ask:
1. **Name** — what is this signal? (e.g., "IMU accelerometer Z-axis", "thermistor on motor housing")
2. **Physical quantity** — what does it measure in the world? (e.g., "vertical acceleration", "motor bearing temperature")
3. **Unit** — (e.g., m/s², °C, Pa, Hz, counts)
4. **Expected range** — min and max in normal operation (e.g., "−2g to +6g during walking")
5. **Hard limits** — values that indicate sensor failure or out-of-range condition
6. **Sample rate** — Hz or trigger condition
7. **Domain primitive link** — which of the device's domain primitives does this signal serve?

---

## Step 3 — Domain primitive extraction

After the signal inventory, derive the domain primitives.

Rules for primitive extraction:
- A domain primitive is a physically measurable quantity the device ultimately reports or controls
- It is NOT a sensor reading — it is what the sensor reading is *evidence of*
- There are usually 2–3 primitives; more than 4 is a sign the scope is too broad
- Every signal collected in Step 2 must trace to at least one primitive
- Flag any signal whose derivation from a domain primitive passes through more than one intermediate physical quantity. The one-intermediate-step limit enforces three properties simultaneously: (1) **Article I traceability** — the primitive citation remains verifiable; (2) **causation over correlation** — each additional intermediate is a potential confound that may correlate with the primitive in the training population but not causally link to it across conditions; (3) **hallucination prevention** — longer chains give an agent room to insert plausible-sounding intermediates that are not actually measured, anchoring decisions in fiction rather than physics. Recommend the human engineer identify a more direct sensor or redefine the primitive.

Present the extracted primitives to the human and ask for confirmation:

```
Based on your answers, the domain primitives for [Device Name] are:

  1. [Primitive name] ([unit]) — [one-line physical description]
     Measured via: [signal(s) from Step 2]

  2. [Primitive name] ([unit]) — [one-line physical description]
     Measured via: [signal(s)]

  3. [Primitive name] ([unit]) — [one-line physical description, if applicable]
     Measured via: [signal(s)]

Do these correctly name what the device ultimately measures or controls?
If no, tell me what to change.
```

Do not proceed to Step 4 until the human confirms the primitives.

---

## Step 4 — Operating envelope

Ask:

**Q6 — Normal operating conditions**
(Temperature range, humidity, vibration, mounting position, use duration, duty cycle)

**Q7 — Worst-case operating conditions**
(The environment the device will encounter at the extremes of its intended use)

**Q8 — Out-of-scope conditions**
(Conditions the device is explicitly NOT designed to handle — what would void the warranty)

---

## Step 5 — Write to docs/device_context.md

Once all answers are collected, write the Device Purpose section of `docs/device_context.md`.

Write the following blocks:

### Device Purpose block
```markdown
## Device Purpose

[One paragraph composed from Q1–Q4 answers. Must name: what the device does,
who depends on it, the hardest scenario (project target), and both failure modes
with their consequences.]

**Project target:** [Q3 answer in one sentence — the specific hard case]

**Pass/fail threshold:** [Q5 answer]

**Domain primitives** (traces to Article I):
1. [Primitive 1] ([unit]) — [description]
   Measured via: [signal(s)]
2. [Primitive 2] ([unit]) — [description]
   Measured via: [signal(s)]
3. [Primitive 3] ([unit]) — [description, if applicable]
   Measured via: [signal(s)]

**Operating envelope:**
- Normal: [Q6 answer]
- Worst-case: [Q7 answer]
- Out-of-scope: [Q8 answer]
```

### Signal Inventory block
Write a Signal Inventory section to `docs/device_context.md`:

```markdown
## Signal Inventory

| Signal | Physical quantity | Unit | Normal range | Hard limits | Sample rate | Primitive |
|--------|-----------------|------|--------------|-------------|-------------|-----------|
| [name] | [quantity]       | [u]  | [min – max]  | [limits]    | [Hz]        | [P1/P2/P3] |
```

---

## Step 6 — Draft Amendment 1

After writing to device_context.md, draft Amendment 1 for the human to ratify.

Print the draft — do NOT write it to amendments.md yet. The human ratifies it explicitly.

```
### PROPOSED AMENDMENT 1: Domain Primitives — [Device Name]
Proposed by: spec-collector
Date: [today]
Traces to: Article I

Governing rule (one sentence):
Every threshold, filter cutoff, FSM transition, and algorithm parameter in this
project must trace to one of the following domain primitives. A parameter that
cannot be so traced is a guess and is not permitted.

Domain primitives:
  1. [Primitive 1] ([unit]) — [description]
  2. [Primitive 2] ([unit]) — [description]
  3. [Primitive 3] ([unit]) — [description, if applicable]

Physical or process justification:
[One paragraph: why these primitives and not others. Cite the project target
and the hardest operating scenario as the justification.]

Amendment it complements or constrains:
  Precedes all other Amendments — all subsequent Amendments must be consistent
  with these primitives.

What happens without it:
  Parameters are set by intuition or by fitting to data, with no traceable
  physical basis. Article I cannot be enforced.
```

Ask the human: "Do you ratify Amendment 1? (yes / no / revise)"
- If yes: write the amendment to `docs/governance/amendments.md` and print a confirmation.
- If revise: ask what to change, revise, and ask again.
- If no: discard and note that Amendment 1 must be ratified before /session 0 can run.

---

## Step 7 — Print readiness summary

```
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
SPEC COLLECTION COMPLETE
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Device Purpose    : written to docs/device_context.md ✓
Signal Inventory  : [N] signals recorded ✓
Domain Primitives : [N] primitives extracted ✓
Amendment 1       : [RATIFIED / PENDING RATIFICATION]
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
Next steps:
  1. Run /toolchain init  — register hardware, pins, and libraries
  2. Ratify Amendments 2–4 (Stage Gate, Toolchain Alignment, Three-Strike)
  3. Run /session 0       — HIL Toolchain Lock
══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════
```

---

## Subcommand: /spec review

Read `docs/device_context.md` and check for gaps. Flag:

- **MISSING** — section is a placeholder, not filled in
- **VAGUE** — Device Purpose has no specific project target or failure mode consequences
- **NO THRESHOLD** — pass/fail threshold is missing or stated qualitatively ("works well")
- **SIGNAL GAP** — a signal is listed in toolchain_config.md (Pin Map) but not in Signal Inventory
- **PRIMITIVE MISMATCH** — a signal's Primitive column does not match any named primitive
- **STALE** — Operating Envelope references conditions that conflict with current toolchain_config.md

Print a gap table, then state which gaps block /session 0 (hard blockers) vs which are warnings.

---

## Subcommand: /spec signals

Skip the full interview. Ask for additional signals to add to the Signal Inventory table in
`docs/device_context.md`. Use the same per-signal questions from Step 2.
Write to the table and confirm what was added.

---

## Subcommand: /spec target

Read the current Device Purpose section. Ask:
"What has changed about the project target since this was written?"
Update only the Project Target and Pass/Fail Threshold lines.
Do not re-interview on primitives or signals unless the human says the target change
requires primitive changes (which would require Amendment revision).

Now parse "collect" and run the matching subcommand, defaulting to `collect` if empty.

lastPrompt: Distinguishing a fall from a dropped object; Distinguishing a fall from heavy footsteps or jumping; it will be targeted for bathroom for now, a far fall vs a close foot step; and most importantly, a h…

content.text:
Captured — bathroom deployment, and three discrimination problems:
1. **Far human fall vs. close footstep** — both can produce similar peak amplitude at the sensor, since attenuation through floor compensates for the larger source energy of a fall.
2. **Dropped object vs. fall** — single brief impact vs. compound impact (limbs + torso + head can hit in sequence).
3. **Slow controlled descent / slump** — the hard one. A frail elderly person "lowering themselves" or sliding down a wall produces **low peak amplitude but extended duration vibration**, which a peak-detector would miss entirely. The signature is likely *cumulative vibration energy over a longer window* and *sustained low-frequency floor flex*, not a single impact spike.

This is a real Article I problem to remember — the algorithm cannot rely on impact amplitude alone. Energy integration over a time window is going to be central.

---

**Q4 — What does failure look like, in both directions?**

- **False positive** (device says "fall" when no fall happened — e.g., dropped shampoo bottle, heavy footstep): device prompts the elderly person → they say "no" → escalation does not fire. What's the *cost* of this happening repeatedly? (Alert fatigue → user disables the device? Or just a minor annoyance?)

- **False negative** (device misses a real fall — e.g., slow slump onto bath mat): elderly person is on the floor, possibly injured, **no prompt fires**, no escalation. They lie there until someone finds them. What's the cost / acceptable rate of this?

Which failure mode is worse for your target user, and is one of them an absolute deal-breaker?

message.content: FP:says fall but a foot step or something dropped. FN: elderly really fell and fainted but no alarm were sound

content.text:
Got it. Standard for medical-alert devices: **FN (missed fall) is almost always worse than FP (false alarm)** — an unconscious elderly person on a bathroom floor is the catastrophic outcome; a few false prompts a week is annoying but recoverable, since the user can dismiss them.

Confirming: do you agree the algorithm should be biased toward sensitivity (catch every real fall, even at the cost of some false alarms)? Or do you have a specific reason to weight them more evenly (e.g., user will rip the device off the wall after 3 false alarms)?

If yes to the standard ranking, I'll move to **Q5 — pass/fail threshold**. For fall detection, this is typically expressed as a pair:
- **Sensitivity target**: e.g., "≥ 95% of real falls detected within 10 s of impact"
- **False positive rate target**: e.g., "≤ 1 false alarm per 24 h of typical bathroom use"

What numbers are you committing to? If you don't have research-backed numbers yet, give me the back-of-envelope target you'd consider "useful enough to deploy" — we can sharpen it later via Amendment.

message.content: I think it should have as little FN as possible, but FP will make elderly very annoyed, so 1 in a week is probably acceptable

content.text:
Clear ranking. Let me propose a concrete Q5 pass/fail threshold and you tell me whether to lock it in or revise:

**Proposed pass/fail threshold:**
- **Sensitivity:** ≥ 95% of real falls detected within 10 seconds of impact (across all three hard scenarios — fast fall, slump, far-from-sensor fall)
- **False positive rate:** ≤ 1 false alarm per 7 days of typical bathroom use
- **Detection latency:** alarm prompt fires within 10 s of fall onset (so a fainted person isn't waiting minutes for help)

The 95% sensitivity is consistent with published medical fall-detector targets; going to 98–99% is possible but usually trades off against FP rate, which conflicts with your "≤1/week" budget. The 10-second latency is what gives the prompt-then-escalate flow time to fire if the user is unconscious.

**Ratify these numbers, or adjust?** (e.g., longer latency OK, higher sensitivity, tighter FP budget, etc.)

message.content: longer latency may be ok e.g. 10s vs 30s do not make the helper time effectiveness change too much

content.text:
Good — and longer latency is actually a *gift* to the algorithm: a 30 s detection window lets you integrate cumulative vibration energy for the slow-slump case, which a 10 s window would chop off mid-event.

**Revised pass/fail threshold:**
- **Sensitivity:** ≥ 95% of real falls detected within **30 s** of fall onset (covering fast fall, slow slump, and far-from-sensor cases)
- **False positive rate:** ≤ 1 false alarm per 7 days of typical bathroom use
- **Detection latency:** alarm prompt fires within 30 s of fall onset

Lock this in?

message.content: yes

Locked. Moving to **Step 2 — Signal inventory**.

List all sensors / signal sources on this device. For each, I'll need: physical quantity measured, unit, expected normal range, hard failure limits, and sample rate.

Starting with the obvious one — the piezo sensor itself:

**Piezo floor-vibration sensor — what I need to know:**

1. **Piezo element type:** discrete piezo disc (e.g., 27 mm bender disc, ~few-nF capacitance, lead-zirconate-titanate), piezo film (PVDF strip), or a packaged accelerometer? This drastically changes the unit and the front-end electronics.
2. **Mounted how:** stuck to the floor / under a tile / on a wall / inside an enclosure that sits on the floor?
3. **Front-end electronics:** charge amplifier? Voltage divider? Direct to MCU ADC? Op-amp gain stage with a known transfer function? Or is this still TBD and you want my recommendation?
4. **Output unit at the MCU:** raw ADC counts, voltage (V), or already calibrated to a physical quantity (Pa, m/s², floor-displacement μm)?
5. **Sample rate target:** floor-vibration signatures from human impact have most energy in 5–80 Hz with some content up to 200 Hz, so a target sample rate of ~500–1000 Hz is typical — what are you planning?
6. **Number of piezo elements:** one sensor, or an array (which would let you localize the source)?

Are there **other sensors** beyond the piezo? Specifically:
- A microphone (acoustic event in parallel)?
- A PIR / radar / mmWave for "is someone in the bathroom"?
- An IMU on the device itself (to ignore vibrations from someone bumping into the device)?

Answer what you know; for items still TBD, say "TBD" and I'll flag them as gaps for `/spec review` later.

**Baseline sensors (confirmed in scope):**

Three focused questions to fill the table:

**A. Piezo front-end → what does the MCU actually see?**
- (a) Raw piezo across a high-Z load → straight into MCU ADC (signal will be bipolar ~±few-V transients, you'll need to bias to mid-rail) → ADC counts
- (b) Charge amplifier or op-amp gain stage with known gain → ADC counts → derivable to voltage (V) or floor-acceleration (m/s²)
- (c) Still TBD — you want me to flag this and decide at `/toolchain init`

**B. Microphone type & MCU interface?**
- (a) Analog electret + amp → MCU ADC
- (b) Digital I2S/PDM MEMS mic (e.g., SPH0645, ICS-43434) — high quality, ~$2

**C. WiFi sensing module output to MCU?**
- (a) Single GPIO line (HIGH = presence)
- (b) UART/I2C message ("presence: 0/1" + confidence)
- (c) Raw CSI stream the MCU has to process (heavy)
- (d) TBD

Pick a letter for each, or say "TBD" — I'll write `TBD` into the inventory and `/spec review` will flag it before Stage 0.

1	# PVDF Piezoelectric Acquisition Circuit — Repository Summary
2	
3	## Overview
4	
5	This repository is a hardware + firmware project for acquiring weak signals from **PVDF (polyvinylidene fluoride) piezoelectric sensors**. It contains analog signal-conditioning circuitry, a PCB design, STM32-based firmware that samples the conditioned signal and displays the waveform on an OLED, plus a collection of reference literature (mainly on fault diagnosis / pulse detection / energy harvesting using PVDF and on signal-processing methods such as EMD and VMD).
6	
7	All original filenames are in Chinese; this document summarizes them in English.
8	
9	## Top-Level Layout
10	
11	```
12	PVDF压电采集资料/                 # "PVDF Piezoelectric Acquisition Materials"
13	├── 10路PVDF采集/                # 10-channel PVDF acquisition board
14	├── PVDF压电采集系统资料/        # Main 1-channel PVDF conditioning system
15	├── 采集代码/                    # STM32 firmware (duplicate / main copy)
16	├── PVDF多路采集.docx            # Multi-channel design notes
17	├── TPS5430.zip                  # Reference design for TPS5430 DC-DC
18	├── 陷波器仿真.ms14              # Multisim notch-filter simulation
19	└── 基于PVDF的动态脉搏检测系统设计_岳晨飞.caj   # Reference thesis
20	```
21	
22	## 1. Signal-Conditioning Hardware
23	
24	### 1.1 Single-channel board — `PVDF压电采集系统资料/`
25	- **Schematic**: `Schematic_PVDF压电信号调理系统_2023-02-20.pdf`
26	- **Gerber files**: `Gerber_PCB_PVDF压电信号调理系统.zip`
27	- **Project source**: `PVDF压电信号调理系统/*.json` (EasyEDA / LCEDA format)
28	- **BOM**: `BOM_PVDF压电信号调理系统_2023-02-20.csv`
29	
30	Key components (from BOM):
31	| Part | Role |
32	|------|------|
33	| **STM32F103C8T6** | MCU (LQFP-48, 8 MHz crystal) |
34	| **MAX44248** | Low-noise precision op-amp (front-end) |
35	| **OP07** | Precision op-amp stage |
36	| **TL072 / LF353** | General-purpose JFET op-amps |
37	| **LM311** | Comparator |
38	| **HCNR200-500E** | Linear optocoupler (isolation) |
39	| **MP2315** | Step-down DC/DC converter |
40	| **AMS1117-3.3** | 3.3 V LDO |
41	| **0.96" OLED (I²C)** | Waveform / voltage display |
42	| **100 MΩ bias (R48)** | High-impedance PVDF input bias |
43	
44	Supporting datasheets included: `C1508997_OP07`, `C23785_HCNR200-500E`, `C51661_降压型` (MP2315 buck), `lm311.pdf`, `tl072.pdf`.
45	
46	### 1.2 Ten-channel board — `10路PVDF采集/`
47	- **Schematic**: `Schematic_10通道PVDF采集调理电路_2023-03-31.pdf`
48	- **Gerber**: `Gerber_PCB_10通道PVDF采集调理电路.zip`
49	- **Source**: `电路设计源文件/10通道PVDF采集调理电路.json`
50	- Uses **CA3140** (MOSFET-input op-amp, ideal for high-impedance PVDF) and **OP07DN** across 10 parallel channels.
51	- Layout image reference: `设计图片.docx`.
52	
53	### 1.3 Notch-filter simulation
54	`陷波器仿真.ms14` — a Multisim 14 simulation of a 50 Hz notch filter to reject mains interference, supporting the reference paper *"Notch-filter suppression of power-line interference on the NI ELVIS II platform"*.
55	
56	## 2. Firmware — `采集代码/` (STM32F103)
57	
58	Target: **STM32F103 ("战舰" / Alientek Warship dev board)**, toolchain Keil MDK (project `Template.uvprojx`).
59	
60	Standard Alientek project layout:
61	```
62	采集代码/
63	├── USER/     main.c, stm32f10x_it.c, system_stm32f10x.c, project files
64	├── HARDWARE/ ADC, AdvancedTim, LED, OLED, OLED0561, SysTick, USART, i2c
65	├── SYSTEM/   delay, sys, usart helpers
66	├── STM32F10x_FWLib/   ST Standard Peripheral Library
67	├── CORE/     CMSIS (core_cm3, startup)
68	└── OBJ/      build outputs (.axf, .hex, ...)
69	```
70	
71	### What `main.c` does
72	1. Init: LED, external-interrupt key, delay, OLED, ADC.
73	2. Sampling constant: `accur = 0.015295` (= `18 × 3.3/4096`, i.e. 3.3 V / 12-bit ADC scaled by an 18× analog gain).
74	3. Main loop toggles between two modes via an interrupt flag `INT_MARK`:
75	   - **Waveform mode** — plots `ConvData` across a 128-pixel OLED screen using `OLED_DrawWave`.
76	   - **Voltage mode** — prints `voltage:%1.3fV` centred around a 1890-count zero-offset: `f = (ConvData − 1890) × 3.3 / 4095`.
77	4. Uses NVIC priority group 2 for interrupt priorities.
78	
79	There is effectively a **duplicate firmware tree** at `PVDF压电采集资料/PVDF压电采集系统资料/采集代码/` containing build artefacts (`.o`, `.crf`, `.d`, `Template.axf`, `Template.hex`). The README inside is the standard Alientek Warship-board boilerplate (UART1 @ 115200, CH340 USB-serial).
80	
81	## 3. Reference Literature (PDF / CAJ)
82	
83	### Application papers
84	- *Active-Matrix Sensing Array Assisted with Machine-Learning for Lumbar Degenerative Disease Diagnosis* (PDF, English).
85	- *Design and Testing of Cantilevered PVDF Energy Harvester Based on the Coanda Effect* (PDF, English).
86	- *可穿戴脉搏检测与心血管疾病诊断系统* — Wearable pulse-detection & cardiovascular diagnosis system (Chen Lu).
87	- *基于PVDF的动态脉搏检测系统设计* — PVDF dynamic pulse-detection system design (Yue Chenfei).
88	- *基于力平衡反馈的压电地震检波器研究* — Force-balance-feedback piezoelectric seismic geophone study (Li Yongchao).
89	- *基于微纳能源采集的智能传感技术研究* — Micro/nano energy-harvesting smart-sensor study (Wen Danliang).
90	- *基于 NI ELVIS II 平台的 Notch 滤波器抑制工频干扰实验* — 50 Hz notch-filter lab on NI ELVIS II.
91	
92	### Signal-processing methods
93	`EMD/` — Empirical Mode Decomposition papers:
94	- EMD + spectral kurtosis envelope analysis for rolling-bearing fault detection.
95	- EMD envelope-spectrum + PCA-PNN for rolling-bearing diagnosis.
96	- EMD full-vector spectrum for sliding-bearing diagnosis.
97	
98	`VMD/` — Variational Mode Decomposition papers:
99	- Optimal IMF + K-S distance for rolling-bearing acoustic fault feature extraction.
100	- Parameter-optimized VMD + multiscale permutation entropy for gear fault diagnosis.
101	- VMD + multiscale permutation entropy + SVM for marine air-compressor fault diagnosis.
102	
103	## 4. How the Pieces Fit Together
104	
105	```
106	   PVDF sensor ─► front-end op-amp (MAX44248 / CA3140, 100 MΩ bias)
107	       ─► gain / filter stages (OP07, TL072, LF353)
108	       ─► 50 Hz notch (Multisim-simulated)
109	       ─► comparator (LM311) / isolation (HCNR200)
110	       ─► STM32F103 ADC (12-bit, ×18 gain scale factor)
111	       ─► OLED display (I²C, 0.96")   + optional UART debug @ 115200
112	```
113	
114	Power: 12 V DC input → **MP2315** buck → **AMS1117-3.3** LDO → MCU / digital rail; TPS5430 reference design kept separately as an alternative DC-DC.
115	
116	## 5. Notes / Gotchas
117	
118	- BOM CSV is UTF-16 encoded (hence the spaced-out glyphs when read as ASCII); open it with UTF-16 or in a spreadsheet app.
119	- The tree contains build artefacts and a Word lock file (`~$DF多路采集.docx`) — safe to ignore / clean.
120	- Two near-identical firmware copies exist; the `采集代码/` folder at the top level appears to be the source of truth, while the nested one contains a previously built binary.
121	- No git history, no license file, no automated build scripts — builds are done from Keil μVision.

├── HARDWARE/ ADC, AdvancedTim, LED, OLED, OLED0561, SysTick, USART, i2c
├── SYSTEM/   delay, sys, usart helpers
├── STM32F10x_FWLib/   ST Standard Peripheral Library
├── CORE/     CMSIS (core_cm3, startup)
└── OBJ/      build outputs (.axf, .hex, ...)
```

### What `main.c` does
1. Init: LED, external-interrupt key, delay, OLED, ADC.
2. Sampling constant: `accur = 0.015295` (= `18 × 3.3/4096`, i.e. 3.3 V / 12-bit ADC scaled by an 18× analog gain).
3. Main loop toggles between two modes via an interrupt flag `INT_MARK`:
   - **Waveform mode** — plots `ConvData` across a 128-pixel OLED screen using `OLED_DrawWave`.
   - **Voltage mode** — prints `voltage:%1.3fV` centred around a 1890-count zero-offset: `f = (ConvData − 1890) × 3.3 / 4095`.
4. Uses NVIC priority group 2 for interrupt priorities.

There is effectively a **duplicate firmware tree** at `PVDF压电采集资料/PVDF压电采集系统资料/采集代码/` containing build artefacts (`.o`, `.crf`, `.d`, `Template.axf`, `Template.hex`). The README inside is the standard Alientek Warship-board boilerplate (UART1 @ 115200, CH340 USB-serial).

## 3. Reference Literature (PDF / CAJ)

### Application papers
- *Active-Matrix Sensing Array Assisted with Machine-Learning for Lumbar Degenerative Disease Diagnosis* (PDF, English).
- *Design and Testing of Cantilevered PVDF Energy Harvester Based on the Coanda Effect* (PDF, English).
- *可穿戴脉搏检测与心血管疾病诊断系统* — Wearable pulse-detection & cardiovascular diagnosis system (Chen Lu).
- *基于PVDF的动态脉搏检测系统设计* — PVDF dynamic pulse-detection system design (Yue Chenfei).
- *基于力平衡反馈的压电地震检波器研究* — Force-balance-feedback piezoelectric seismic geophone study (Li Yongchao).
- *基于微纳能源采集的智能传感技术研究* — Micro/nano energy-harvesting smart-sensor study (Wen Danliang).
- *基于 NI ELVIS II 平台的 Notch 滤波器抑制工频干扰实验* — 50 Hz notch-filter lab on NI ELVIS II.

### Signal-processing methods
`EMD/` — Empirical Mode Decomposition papers:
- EMD + spectral kurtosis envelope analysis for rolling-bearing fault detection.
- EMD envelope-spectrum + PCA-PNN for rolling-bearing diagnosis.
- EMD full-vector spectrum for sliding-bearing diagnosis.

`VMD/` — Variational Mode Decomposition papers:
- Optimal IMF + K-S distance for rolling-bearing acoustic fault feature extraction.
- Parameter-optimized VMD + multiscale permutation entropy for gear fault diagnosis.
- VMD + multiscale permutation entropy + SVM for marine air-compressor fault diagnosis.

## 4. How the Pieces Fit Together

```
   PVDF sensor ─► front-end op-amp (MAX44248 / CA3140, 100 MΩ bias)
       ─► gain / filter stages (OP07, TL072, LF353)
       ─► 50 Hz notch (Multisim-simulated)
       ─► comparator (LM311) / isolation (HCNR200)
       ─► STM32F103 ADC (12-bit, ×18 gain scale factor)
       ─► OLED display (I²C, 0.96")   + optional UART debug @ 115200
```

Power: 12 V DC input → **MP2315** buck → **AMS1117-3.3** LDO → MCU / digital rail; TPS5430 reference design kept separately as an alternative DC-DC.

## 5. Notes / Gotchas

- BOM CSV is UTF-16 encoded (hence the spaced-out glyphs when read as ASCII); open it with UTF-16 or in a spreadsheet app.
- The tree contains build artefacts and a Word lock file (`~$DF多路采集.docx`) — safe to ignore / clean.
- Two near-identical firmware copies exist; the `采集代码/` folder at the top level appears to be the source of truth, while the nested one contains a previously built binary.
- No git history, no license file, no automated build scripts — builds are done from Keil μVision.

132	                           │

135	                                          RP4 100k trim)

205	### C.1 Architecture

210	 P1 (screw terminal)  ──► switch (102 kind, 3-pos) ──► TPS5430 dual module (M1)
211	                                                      │

214	                                                      └─ −15 V ─┘

216	 For each of channels 1…10  (U1+U2, U3+U4, … , U19+U20):
217	
218	   Sensor input Dn (KF301-5.0 screw terminal)
219	      │
220	      ▼

222	      │         Feedback: R-n 100 MΩ ‖ C-n 10 nF  (103)
223	      │         ⇒ Charge amplifier:  V_out = − Q_sensor / C_f
224	      │         (high-pass corner  f_HP = 1/(2π · 100 MΩ · 10 nF) ≈ 0.16 Hz)
225	      ▼
226	   OP07CDR    (Un+1, precision inverting gain)
227	      │         Input R: 1 k (R_odd)
228	      │         Feedback: R_even 1 k in series with RP_n (20 k trimpot)
229	      │         ⇒ Gain ≈ −(1 k + RPn)/1 k   (1× to 21×)

288	### D.2 `main.c` — behaviour
289	
290	| Step | Action |
291	|------|--------|
292	| 1 | `LED_Init()`, `INT_INIT()`, `delay_init()` |
293	| 2 | `OLED_Init()` + `OLED_Init2()` — two OLEDs (or two init paths to the same one) |
294	| 3 | `ADCx_Init()` — starts continuous, DMA-driven ADC1 sampling into `ConvData` |
295	| 4 | `NVIC_PriorityGroupConfig(NVIC_PriorityGroup_2)` |
296	| 5 | **Main loop**, toggled by `INT_MARK` (set by the external key / trigger ISR): |
297	| 5a | `INT_MARK == 1` → **waveform mode**: sweep x = 0..127, call `OLED_DrawWave(x, accur*ConvData)` — live trace on the OLED |
298	| 5b | `INT_MARK == 0` → **voltage mode**: compute `f = (ConvData − 1890) × 3.3 / 4095`, clamp ≥0, `sprintf("voltage:%1.3fV")`, display every 200 ms |

300	Calibration constants:
301	- `accur = 0.015295` = `18 × 3.3 / 4096` → assumes a **×18 analog gain** between the sensor and the ADC pin (matches the OP07 + filter chain on Design #1).
302	- Zero code: **1890** → mid-rail bias after AC coupling (the MCU samples a DC-biased AC signal; 1890 ≈ 1.52 V, consistent with an internal 1.5 V bias node).

310	| Mode | `ADC_Mode_Independent`, **continuous** conversion |
311	| Scan | disabled (single channel) |
312	| Data align | right |
313	| Trigger | software (`ADC_SoftwareStartConvCmd`) |
314	| Sample time | **239.5 cycles** (longest available; correct for high-source-impedance OP07 output through a resistor divider) |
315	| ADC clock | `PCLK2/6` (typically 12 MHz if PCLK2 = 72 MHz) |
316	| DMA | DMA1 Channel 1, 16-bit half-word, circular, peripheral → memory → `ConvData` |
317	| Calibration | performed at init |

321	### D.4 `bsp_advanced_timer.c` — TIM1
322	
323	Configured as **complementary PWM (TIM1_CH1 / TIM1_CH1N with break input BKIN)**. Not invoked in the current `main.c` (the call `AdvancedTim_Init()` is commented out). Likely kept for future use — e.g. driving an external DAC / modulation stage on the board.
324	
325	### D.5 OLED and I²C
326	
327	- Two OLED drivers coexist: `OLED_I2C` (primary 0.96″ SSD1306) and `OLED0561` (alternate); `main.c` calls both, suggesting dual-OLED support or build variants.
328	- The single-channel board's P1 header is the physical I²C OLED slot; per hardware schematic, SCL/SDA are pulled up to 3.3 V.
329	
330	### D.6 README (Alientek / "战舰" Warship board)
331	
332	`采集代码/README.TXT` is the stock Alientek boilerplate: USB-UART via CH340 on PA9/PA10, 115200 baud. The project is built against the "Warship V3" dev board pinning; the custom PCB (§B) reuses the same pinout for drop-in firmware portability.
333	
334	---
335	
336	## E. Reference / Simulation Material
337	
338	| File | Purpose |
339	|------|---------|
340	| `陷波器仿真.ms14` (Multisim 14, binary) | 50 Hz notch-filter simulation; supports 王晓娜's ELVIS II notch-filter paper. **Neither PCB currently has an on-board notch**, so this is design exploration / future rev. |
341	| `TPS5430.zip` | External reference design for the ±15 V module used by the 10-channel board. |
342	| `EMD/*.pdf` | Empirical Mode Decomposition references for bearing-fault vibration analysis. |
343	| `VMD/*.pdf` | Variational Mode Decomposition references (VMD + MPE + SVM, etc.). |
344	| `Active-Matrix Sensing Array … Lumbar … ML Approach.pdf` | Application paper — PVDF array + ML for medical diagnosis. |
345	| `Design_and_Testing_of_Cantilevered_PVDF_Energy_Harvester … Coanda Effect.pdf` | PVDF as energy harvester. |
346	| `可穿戴脉搏检测与心血管疾病诊断系统_陈璐.caj` | Wearable pulse detection / cardiovascular diagnosis thesis. |
347	| `基于PVDF的动态脉搏检测系统设计_岳晨飞.caj` | Closest analogue to this project — PVDF dynamic pulse-detection system. |
348	| `基于力平衡反馈的压电地震检波器研究_李永超.caj` | Piezoelectric seismic geophone study. |
349	| `基于微纳能源采集的智能传感技术研究_文丹良.caj` | Energy-harvesting smart-sensor study. |
350	| `基于NI_ELVISⅡ平台…陷波器抑制工频干扰实验_王晓娜.pdf` | ELVIS II lab on notch-based 50 Hz rejection. |
351	
352	Datasheets retained alongside the schematics:
353	- `C1508997_OP07_2020-12-21.PDF`, `C2902479_OP07DN_2022-01-14.PDF`
354	- `C23785_HCNR200-500E_2016-03-18.PDF` (linear optocoupler; appears in BOM but not obviously in the drawn schematic — likely reserved for an isolation rev)
355	- `C51661_降压型_2015-06-18.PDF` (MP2315 buck family)
356	- `C122729_CA3140EZ_2017-07-19.PDF`
357	- `lm311.pdf`, `tl072.pdf`
358	
359	---
360	
361	## F. Design Comparison (at a glance)
362	
363	| Aspect | Design #1 — single channel + MCU | Design #2 — 10-channel analog |
364	|--------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
365	| Channels | 1 | 10 |
366	| Front-end topology | Voltage pickup (100 MΩ to GND, AC-couple, then TL072 buffer) | Charge amplifier (100 MΩ ‖ 10 nF feedback on CA3140) |
367	| Front-end op-amp | TL072 → MAX44248 (dual low-noise) | CA3140 (MOSFET, 1 per channel) |
368	| Filter stages | 2× LF353 biquads with three 100 k trims | — (none; external DAQ does the filtering) |
369	| Final gain stage | OP07 with ±2 k / 1 k feedback (fixed) | OP07 inverting with 20 k trim per channel |
370	| Trigger output | **LM311 comparator → Dout** | — |
371	| Analog supplies | ±5 V (external via H0) | ±15 V (TPS5430 module) |
372	| Digital supplies | +5 V (MP2315) + 3.3 V (AMS1117) | none |
373	| Digital / compute | **STM32F103C8T6**, ADC1 DMA, UART1, I²C OLED | none |
374	| User I/O | 0.96″ I²C OLED, LEDs, reset/boot buttons | none (bench instrument drives the header) |
375	| Input connector | 1×2 pin header (H1) | 10× KF301 screw terminals (D1–D10) |
376	| Output connector | USB-UART + on-board ADC/OLED | 1×10 header (H4) to external DAQ |
377	| Intended use | **All-in-one benchtop PVDF monitor** | **Sensor-array front-end feeding external DAQ** |
378	
379	---
380	
381	## G. Gotchas / Things to Check Before Manufacturing
382	
383	1. **High-impedance nodes** (100 MΩ on both boards): guard rings, clean flux-free soldering, optionally conformal coat. Humidity and dirty boards will shift gain and drift.
384	2. **Gain calibration** — the 10-channel board's ten trimpots must be set against a reference before any cross-channel comparison is meaningful; plan a calibration fixture.
385	3. **No mains-frequency rejection on either PCB** — the `陷波器仿真.ms14` twin-T notch is a planned addition. Until fitted, expect 50 Hz pickup on the sensor leads.
386	4. **Shielding** — PVDF leads pick up capacitively from anything within ~10 cm. Use coax with shield tied only at the amp end (J2 on design #2).
387	5. **TVS coverage** — design #1 has SMAJ12A at the 12 V jack; design #2 has **no** input protection on the sensor terminals. Consider back-to-back TVS / bidirectional clamp diodes on each Dn if the sensors can see mechanical shock.
388	6. **Ground strategy** — design #1 ties analog and digital grounds at a single point on the PCB (inspect Gerbers to confirm). A true split-plane layout would help at µV levels.
389	7. **`HCNR200` in BOM but not on the drawn sheet** — probably laid out on an unused pad or reserved for an isolated-output rev; confirm against the Gerbers before stuffing.
390	8. **Dual OLED init in `main.c`** (`OLED_Init()` and `OLED_Init2()`) — confirm the target board only has one OLED mounted, or you'll stall on a non-responding bus.
391	9. **Fixed `1890` zero-code in firmware** — this is a hand-calibrated DC-bias number for one specific unit; re-measure after any change to the analog rails or R43/R44 ratio.
392	10. **File encoding** — the BOM CSV is UTF-16; open with a spreadsheet app (Excel / LibreOffice) rather than a text editor.
393	
394	---
395	
396	## H. Suggested Next Steps (if you're iterating the design)
397	
398	1. Render the PCB top/bottom layers out of the `*.json` LCEDA files (open on oshwhub.com) and add them here alongside the schematic images.
399	2. Add an on-board twin-T 50 Hz notch (port the Multisim design) between the filter bank and the ADC / output header.
400	3. Add input protection (back-to-back TVS + RC) to each sensor input on the 10-channel board.
401	4. Replace the fixed `1890` bias in firmware with a one-time self-calibration at startup (sample N conversions with input grounded, store offset).
402	5. Expose ADC values over UART or USB-CDC so you can log to PC during bench work — the STM32F103 already has the UART configured at 115200 baud.
403

    │   ├── C51661_降压型_2015-06-18 (1).PDF      # MP2315 buck ds

---

## B. Design #1 — Single-Channel PVDF Signal-Conditioning System

**Source files**
- Schematic PDF: [`PVDF压电采集资料/PVDF压电采集系统资料/Schematic_PVDF压电信号调理系统_2023-02-20.pdf`](PVDF压电采集资料/PVDF压电采集系统资料/Schematic_PVDF压电信号调理系统_2023-02-20.pdf)
- Rendered image below (full page):

![Single-channel PVDF conditioning system — schematic](images/schematic_1ch-1.png)

- Editable source: `PVDF压电采集资料/PVDF压电采集系统资料/PVDF压电信号调理系统/PVDF压电信号调理系统.json` (LCEDA)
- PCB source: `…/PCB_PVDF压电信号调理系统.json`
- Gerbers: `Gerber_PCB_PVDF压电信号调理系统.zip`
- BOM: `BOM_PVDF压电信号调理系统_2023-02-20.csv` (57 line items; UTF-16 encoding)

### B.1 Board-level block diagram

```
 +12 V IN (J1, DC-470 jack)
   ├── TVS SMAJ12A (D1)        ─ surge clamp, stand-off 12 V
   ├── Slide switch K1 (MSS22D18G2)
   ├── MP2315 buck  (U2, ±40 V-in SOT23-8)
   │     L1 = 4.7 µH, C5 = 33 pF comp, FB = R6 40.2 k / R7 7.5 k  → +5 V
   ├── AMS1117-3.3 LDO (U3)                                        → +3.3 V
   └── External ±5 V comes in via H0 (1×4 header) — feeds the op-amp rails

 PVDF sensor  (H1, 1×2 header)
   → front-end analog chain (section B.3)
   → Aout → STM32 ADC pin
   → Dout (LM311 output) → STM32 GPIO (EXTI trigger)

 STM32F103C8T6 (U15, LQFP-48)
   ├── 8 MHz xtal X2 + 22 pF C11/C12
   ├── VDD decoupling: C16, C17, C18, C49, C53  (0.1 µF)
   ├── NRST pull-up R12 10 k + reset button (H2 implicit)
   ├── BOOT0 / TX1 / RX1 on H15 (1×4)
   ├── Programming/debug fan-out H6 (1×6): PA11, PA4, PA2, PA3, GND, 5V
   ├── I²C1 → OLED P1 (pull-ups R58/R59 5.1 k to 3.3 V)
   └── Status LEDs LED1 (3.3 V rail), LED4 (5 V rail), LED5 (Dout)
```

### B.2 Power-supply detail

| Rail | Source | Key components | Notes |
|------|--------|---------------|-------|
| +12 V | Barrel jack (DC-470-2.1GP) | D1 SMAJ12A TVS, K1 slide switch | Reverse-polarity protection optional |
| +5 V (dig/analog) | MP2315 step-down | L1 4.7 µH; C6 22 µF + C7 22 µF + C10 22 µF out caps; EN via R1/R2 | `Vout = 0.8 V × (1 + R6/R7) ≈ 5.09 V` |
| +3.3 V | AMS1117-3.3 | C9 10 µF in, C14 / C8 / C53 / C49 decoupling | MCU + OLED |
| ±5 V (analog) | external (H0 header) | C33/C34 100 µF, C35–C38 0.1 µF/10 nF | Rails for all op-amps |

### B.3 Analog signal chain (bottom band of schematic)

The chain is built as a **buffered → low-noise precision → active-filter → gain-trim → precision output → comparator-trigger** topology.

```
PVDF(H1) ── R47 4.7k ──┬── 100 MΩ (R48, 2512 SMD)
                       │       to GND  (DC bias / leakage for high-Z film)
                       └── C43 1 µF (105)   AC-couple
                           │
                           ▼
  U14.1  TL072IDR   ── JFET-input buffer  (Zin ≈ 10¹² Ω)
                           │
                           ▼
  U1.2   MAX44248     low-noise precision stage  (eN ≈ 5.8 nV/√Hz)
                           │
                           ▼
  U1.1   MAX44248     second precision stage
                           │
                           ▼
  U13    LF353        active filter A   (33 nF caps C15/C26/C41/C42;
                                          5.1 k / 91 k / 43 k ladder;
                                          RP2 100k, RP3 100k trim)
                           │
                           ▼
  U8     LF353        active filter B   (33 nF C29–C32; mirror of A;
                                          RP4 100k trim)
                           │
                           ▼
  U9     OP07CSZ      DC-accurate output gain
                      (R43 5k / R44 5k, C13 / C40 0.2 µF, R45 1k / R46 2k)
                           │
                  ┌────────┴─────────┐
                  │                  │
         H3/H4 test header     R9/R10/R11/R12/R13/R14 divider
                                     │
                                     ▼
                             Aout → STM32 ADC (PA6 per firmware)
                  ┌──────── also to ────────┐
                  ▼
  U16    LM311DR   comparator
         threshold: R64 100k / RP5 100k / R63 1k
                           │
                           ▼
                     Dout → STM32 GPIO (event trigger)
                     LED5 mirrors the comparator state
```

**Why these parts:**
- **R48 = 100 MΩ** — PVDF film behaves like a tiny capacitor; without a DC path, op-amp bias currents would walk the input to a rail. The extra-high value keeps the −3 dB corner at sub-1 Hz for a few-nF film.
- **MAX44248** — dual, 0.045 µV/°C offset drift, 5.8 nV/√Hz. Good for µV-range conditioning.
- **LF353 × 2** with multi-turn **RP2/RP3/RP4** — two cascaded biquad-style filters whose centre frequency and Q can be trimmed on the bench.
- **OP07** — ultra-low-offset precision gain; feeds ADC and comparator.
- **LM311** — open-collector comparator driving a GPIO; optional digital trigger path.

### B.4 Microcontroller pinout (from the PDF + firmware)

| STM32 pin | Signal | Destination |
|-----------|--------|-------------|
| PA6 (ADC1_IN6) | Aout | Analog output of OP07 U9 (see `bsp_adc.h`) |
| PA9 / PA10 | UART1 TX / RX | Header H15 (debug / serial logging) |
| PA11 | GPIO | Header H6 (general I/O) |
| PA2 / PA3 / PA4 | GPIO | Header H6 |
| PB6 / PB7 | I²C1 SCL / SDA | OLED P1, pulled up 5.1 k (firmware uses software I²C on different pins — see §D) |
| PB15 | GPIO | Dout from LM311 (EXTI trigger) |
| NRST / BOOT0 | Reset / boot | RST button + H15 |
| OSC_IN / OSC_OUT | 8 MHz xtal | X2 + C11/C12 22 pF |

### B.5 Connectors

| Ref | Function | Pinout |
|-----|----------|--------|
| J1 | DC input | 12 V barrel |
| H0 | External ±5 V + signals | GND, +5V, −5V, Dout |
| H1 | PVDF sensor | 1×2 |
| H2–H5 | Test points | 1×2 each (Aout taps, GND) |
| H6 | MCU fan-out | PA11, PA4, PA2, PA3, GND, 5V |
| H15 | UART + boot | TX1, BOOT0, RX1, GND |
| H16 | Misc I/O | 1×3 |
| P1 | OLED 0.96″ I²C | GND, VCC, SCL, SDA |

---

## C. Design #2 — 10-Channel PVDF Acquisition / Conditioning Board

**Source files**
- Schematic PDF: [`PVDF压电采集资料/10路PVDF采集/Schematic_10通道PVDF采集调理电路_2023-03-31.pdf`](PVDF压电采集资料/10路PVDF采集/Schematic_10通道PVDF采集调理电路_2023-03-31.pdf)
- Rendered image below (full page):

![Ten-channel PVDF front-end — schematic](images/schematic_10ch-1.png)

- Editable source: `10路PVDF采集/电路设计源文件/10通道PVDF采集调理电路.json`
- PCB source: `…/PCB_10通道PVDF采集调理电路.json`
- Gerbers: `Gerber_PCB_10通道PVDF采集调理电路.zip`
- Design reference photo: `设计图片.docx`

### C.1 Architecture

A **pure-analog, 10-identical-channel** charge-amplifier front-end. No MCU, no ADC — signals exit on a single 10-pin header for external digitization.

```
 P1 (screw terminal)  ──► switch (102 kind, 3-pos) ──► TPS5430 dual module (M1)
                                                      │
                                                      ├─ +15 V ─┐
                                                      ├─  GND  ─┤ to all 20 op-amps
                                                      └─ −15 V ─┘

 For each of channels 1…10  (U1+U2, U3+U4, … , U19+U20):

   Sensor input Dn (KF301-5.0 screw terminal)
      │
      ▼
   CA3140AMZ  (Un, MOSFET input, Ib ≈ 1.5 pA)
      │         Feedback: R-n 100 MΩ ‖ C-n 10 nF  (103)
      │         ⇒ Charge amplifier:  V_out = − Q_sensor / C_f
      │         (high-pass corner  f_HP = 1/(2π · 100 MΩ · 10 nF) ≈ 0.16 Hz)
      ▼
   OP07CDR    (Un+1, precision inverting gain)
      │         Input R: 1 k (R_odd)
      │         Feedback: R_even 1 k in series with RP_n (20 k trimpot)
      │         ⇒ Gain ≈ −(1 k + RPn)/1 k   (1× to 21×)
      ▼
   Channel output  A_n  →  10-pin header H4

 H4 (1×10 female header) pins 1…10  = channels A1…A10
 J2 (single pin)                      = shield / auxiliary GND
```

### C.2 Per-channel part list

| Ref (ch n) | Part | Role |
|------------|------|------|
| Dn | KF301-5.0-2P | Screw-terminal sensor input (+ / shield) |
| Un (odd index) | **CA3140AMZ** | Charge-amp (MOSFET input) |
| R-n | 100 MΩ | Feedback resistor (sets DC gain, ≈ leakage path) |
| C-n | 10 nF (103) | Feedback capacitor (sets charge-to-voltage ratio) |
| R(2n−1) | 1 kΩ | Series input to OP07 |
| R(2n) | 1 kΩ | Base feedback to OP07 |
| RPn | 20 kΩ trimpot | Gain trim for this channel |
| Un+1 (even) | **OP07CDR** | Precision inverting gain |
| Cn / Cn+1 | 0.1 µF (104) | Supply decoupling on each op-amp pin |

(Channels 1–10 instantiate this block verbatim, with part suffixes stepping through the numbering.)

### C.3 Global parts

| Ref | Part | Role |
|-----|------|------|
| M1  | TPS5430-based dual module | ±15 V rail generation |
| P1  | 5.08 mm 2-pin (+ 102 switch) | Raw DC input + power switch |
| H4  | 1×10 female header | 10-channel output to DAQ |
| J2  | 1×1 header | Ground / shield |

### C.4 Design intent

This board is built to feed a 10-input DAQ — e.g. an **NI ELVIS II**, a PCIe DAQ card, or an STM32 with multi-channel DMA-ADC — from a **PVDF sensor array** (think: a row of 10 pressure-sense patches, or 10 accelerometers bonded to a structure). The ±15 V rails (vs the ±5 V on design #1) give every channel more output swing, and the dedicated charge amplifier per channel preserves channel-to-channel isolation.

---

## D. Firmware — `PVDF压电采集资料/采集代码/` (STM32F103C8T6)

**Toolchain:** Keil MDK (`Template.uvprojx`); device uses ST Standard Peripheral Library (not HAL/Cube).

### D.1 Layout

```
USER/                 main.c, stm32f10x_it.c, system_stm32f10x.c, Keil projects
HARDWARE/
  ADC/                bsp_adc.{c,h}              — ADC1 on PA6, CH6, DMA1_Ch1
  AdvancedTim/        bsp_advanced_timer.{c,h}   — TIM1 complementary PWM
  LED/, SysTick/, USART/, i2c/
  OLED/               OLED_I2C.{c,h}, codetab.h  — primary 0.96″ OLED driver
  OLED0561/           second OLED driver (128×64 alternate)
SYSTEM/               delay, sys, usart helpers
STM32F10x_FWLib/      ST SPL
CORE/                 CMSIS + startup_stm32f10x_hd.s
OBJ/                  Keil build output
```

### D.2 `main.c` — behaviour

| Step | Action |
|------|--------|
| 1 | `LED_Init()`, `INT_INIT()`, `delay_init()` |
| 2 | `OLED_Init()` + `OLED_Init2()` — two OLEDs (or two init paths to the same one) |
| 3 | `ADCx_Init()` — starts continuous, DMA-driven ADC1 sampling into `ConvData` |
| 4 | `NVIC_PriorityGroupConfig(NVIC_PriorityGroup_2)` |
| 5 | **Main loop**, toggled by `INT_MARK` (set by the external key / trigger ISR): |
| 5a | `INT_MARK == 1` → **waveform mode**: sweep x = 0..127, call `OLED_DrawWave(x, accur*ConvData)` — live trace on the OLED |
| 5b | `INT_MARK == 0` → **voltage mode**: compute `f = (ConvData − 1890) × 3.3 / 4095`, clamp ≥0, `sprintf("voltage:%1.3fV")`, display every 200 ms |

Calibration constants:
- `accur = 0.015295` = `18 × 3.3 / 4096` → assumes a **×18 analog gain** between the sensor and the ADC pin (matches the OP07 + filter chain on Design #1).
- Zero code: **1890** → mid-rail bias after AC coupling (the MCU samples a DC-biased AC signal; 1890 ≈ 1.52 V, consistent with an internal 1.5 V bias node).

### D.3 `bsp_adc.c/.h` — ADC configuration

| Setting | Value |
|---------|-------|
| ADC | ADC1 |
| GPIO | PA6 (ADC1_IN6) as `GPIO_Mode_AIN` |
| Mode | `ADC_Mode_Independent`, **continuous** conversion |
| Scan | disabled (single channel) |
| Data align | right |
| Trigger | software (`ADC_SoftwareStartConvCmd`) |
| Sample time | **239.5 cycles** (longest available; correct for high-source-impedance OP07 output through a resistor divider) |
| ADC clock | `PCLK2/6` (typically 12 MHz if PCLK2 = 72 MHz) |
| DMA | DMA1 Channel 1, 16-bit half-word, circular, peripheral → memory → `ConvData` |
| Calibration | performed at init |

Effective sample rate ≈ `12 MHz / (239.5 + 12.5) = ~47.6 kS/s` — plenty for PVDF pulse / pulse-rate / speech-band work.

### D.4 `bsp_advanced_timer.c` — TIM1

Configured as **complementary PWM (TIM1_CH1 / TIM1_CH1N with break input BKIN)**. Not invoked in the current `main.c` (the call `AdvancedTim_Init()` is commented out). Likely kept for future use — e.g. driving an external DAC / modulation stage on the board.

### D.5 OLED and I²C

- Two OLED drivers coexist: `OLED_I2C` (primary 0.96″ SSD1306) and `OLED0561` (alternate); `main.c` calls both, suggesting dual-OLED support or build variants.
- The single-channel board's P1 header is the physical I²C OLED slot; per hardware schematic, SCL/SDA are pulled up to 3.3 V.

### D.6 README (Alientek / "战舰" Warship board)

`采集代码/README.TXT` is the stock Alientek boilerplate: USB-UART via CH340 on PA9/PA10, 115200 baud. The project is built against the "Warship V3" dev board pinning; the custom PCB (§B) reuses the same pinout for drop-in firmware portability.

---

## E. Reference / Simulation Material

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `陷波器仿真.ms14` (Multisim 14, binary) | 50 Hz notch-filter simulation; supports 王晓娜's ELVIS II notch-filter paper. **Neither PCB currently has an on-board notch**, so this is design exploration / future rev. |
| `TPS5430.zip` | External reference design for the ±15 V module used by the 10-channel board. |
| `EMD/*.pdf` | Empirical Mode Decomposition references for bearing-fault vibration analysis. |
| `VMD/*.pdf` | Variational Mode Decomposition references (VMD + MPE + SVM, etc.). |
| `Active-Matrix Sensing Array … Lumbar … ML Approach.pdf` | Application paper — PVDF array + ML for medical diagnosis. |
| `Design_and_Testing_of_Cantilevered_PVDF_Energy_Harvester … Coanda Effect.pdf` | PVDF as energy harvester. |
| `可穿戴脉搏检测与心血管疾病诊断系统_陈璐.caj` | Wearable pulse detection / cardiovascular diagnosis thesis. |
| `基于PVDF的动态脉搏检测系统设计_岳晨飞.caj` | Closest analogue to this project — PVDF dynamic pulse-detection system. |
| `基于力平衡反馈的压电地震检波器研究_李永超.caj` | Piezoelectric seismic geophone study. |
| `基于微纳能源采集的智能传感技术研究_文丹良.caj` | Energy-harvesting smart-sensor study. |
| `基于NI_ELVISⅡ平台…陷波器抑制工频干扰实验_王晓娜.pdf` | ELVIS II lab on notch-based 50 Hz rejection. |

Datasheets retained alongside the schematics:
- `C1508997_OP07_2020-12-21.PDF`, `C2902479_OP07DN_2022-01-14.PDF`
- `C23785_HCNR200-500E_2016-03-18.PDF` (linear optocoupler; appears in BOM but not obviously in the drawn schematic — likely reserved for an isolation rev)
- `C51661_降压型_2015-06-18.PDF` (MP2315 buck family)
- `C122729_CA3140EZ_2017-07-19.PDF`
- `lm311.pdf`, `tl072.pdf`

---

## F. Design Comparison (at a glance)

| Aspect | Design #1 — single channel + MCU | Design #2 — 10-channel analog |
|--------|----------------------------------|-------------------------------|
| Channels | 1 | 10 |
| Front-end topology | Voltage pickup (100 MΩ to GND, AC-couple, then TL072 buffer) | Charge amplifier (100 MΩ ‖ 10 nF feedback on CA3140) |
| Front-end op-amp | TL072 → MAX44248 (dual low-noise) | CA3140 (MOSFET, 1 per channel) |
| Filter stages | 2× LF353 biquads with three 100 k trims | — (none; external DAQ does the filtering) |
| Final gain stage | OP07 with ±2 k / 1 k feedback (fixed) | OP07 inverting with 20 k trim per channel |
| Trigger output | **LM311 comparator → Dout** | — |
| Analog supplies | ±5 V (external via H0) | ±15 V (TPS5430 module) |
| Digital supplies | +5 V (MP2315) + 3.3 V (AMS1117) | none |
| Digital / compute | **STM32F103C8T6**, ADC1 DMA, UART1, I²C OLED | none |
| User I/O | 0.96″ I²C OLED, LEDs, reset/boot buttons | none (bench instrument drives the header) |
| Input connector | 1×2 pin header (H1) | 10× KF301 screw terminals (D1–D10) |
| Output connector | USB-UART + on-board ADC/OLED | 1×10 header (H4) to external DAQ |
| Intended use | **All-in-one benchtop PVDF monitor** | **Sensor-array front-end feeding external DAQ** |

---

## G. Gotchas / Things to Check Before Manufacturing

1. **High-impedance nodes** (100 MΩ on both boards): guard rings, clean flux-free soldering, optionally conformal coat. Humidity and dirty boards will shift gain and drift.
2. **Gain calibration** — the 10-channel board's ten trimpots must be set against a reference before any cross-channel comparison is meaningful; plan a calibration fixture.
3. **No mains-frequency rejection on either PCB** — the `陷波器仿真.ms14` twin-T notch is a planned addition. Until fitted, expect 50 Hz pickup on the sensor leads.
4. **Shielding** — PVDF leads pick up capacitively from anything within ~10 cm. Use coax with shield tied only at the amp end (J2 on design #2).
5. **TVS coverage** — design #1 has SMAJ12A at the 12 V jack; design #2 has **no** input protection on the sensor terminals. Consider back-to-back TVS / bidirectional clamp diodes on each Dn if the sensors can see mechanical shock.
6. **Ground strategy** — design #1 ties analog and digital grounds at a single point on the PCB (inspect Gerbers to confirm). A true split-plane layout would help at µV levels.
7. **`HCNR200` in BOM but not on the drawn sheet** — probably laid out on an unused pad or reserved for an isolated-output rev; confirm against the Gerbers before stuffing.
8. **Dual OLED init in `main.c`** (`OLED_Init()` and `OLED_Init2()`) — confirm the target board only has one OLED mounted, or you'll stall on a non-responding bus.
9. **Fixed `1890` zero-code in firmware** — this is a hand-calibrated DC-bias number for one specific unit; re-measure after any change to the analog rails or R43/R44 ratio.
10. **File encoding** — the BOM CSV is UTF-16; open with a spreadsheet app (Excel / LibreOffice) rather than a text editor.

---

## H. Suggested Next Steps (if you're iterating the design)

1. Render the PCB top/bottom layers out of the `*.json` LCEDA files (open on oshwhub.com) and add them here alongside the schematic images.
2. Add an on-board twin-T 50 Hz notch (port the Multisim design) between the filter bank and the ADC / output header.
3. Add input protection (back-to-back TVS + RC) to each sensor input on the 10-channel board.
4. Replace the fixed `1890` bias in firmware with a one-time self-calibration at startup (sample N conversions with input grounded, store offset).
5. Expose ADC values over UART or USB-CDC so you can log to PC during bench work — the STM32F103 already has the UART configured at 115200 baud.
